COLOR_SCHEME_SCRIPT
#

csp.ts view source

"\n\t\t\tdocument.documentElement.classList.add(\n\t\t\t\t((c) =>\n\t\t\t\t\tc === 'dark' || (c !== 'light' && matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme:dark)').matches)\n\t\t\t\t\t\t? 'dark'\n\t\t\t\t\t\t: 'light')(localStorage.getItem('fuz:color-scheme'))\n\t\t\t);\n\t\t"

The exact body of the color-scheme loader <script> in app.html, the inline script COLOR_SCHEME_SCRIPT_HASH admits.

The loader has to run before first paint to avoid a flash of the wrong scheme, so it is inline rather than a render-blocking src, and CSP admits it by hash. That makes its bytes load-bearing: whitespace, quoting, and trailing commas all move the hash, so a formatter that reflows app.html breaks the theme on every cold load with nothing but a console violation to show for it. Consumers can guard their own app.html against this constant.

import {COLOR_SCHEME_SCRIPT} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/csp.ts';

COLOR_SCHEME_SCRIPT_HASH
#

csp.ts view source

"sha256-CkhymyixntvSTuePGizI3BFtnRFlWWg95YBmBOCFxfY="

The sha256- CSP source for COLOR_SCHEME_SCRIPT, carried by the script-src and script-src-elem defaults so the loader runs under the library CSP.

Regenerate after any edit to COLOR_SCHEME_SCRIPT — src/test/csp.color_scheme.test.ts reports the expected value when the two disagree.

import {COLOR_SCHEME_SCRIPT_HASH} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/csp.ts';

contextmenu_calculate_constrained_x(menu_x: number, menu_width: number, layout_width: number): number

Constrains the menu's x coordinate to the layout, shifting left to fit the right edge. Clamps at 0 so a menu wider than the layout pins its left edge - the start of each item stays visible.

contextmenu_calculate_constrained_y(menu_y: number, menu_height: number, layout_height: number): number

Constrains the menu's y coordinate to the layout, shifting up to fit the bottom edge. Clamps at 0 so a menu taller than the layout pins its top edge - the first items stay visible.

import {contextmenu_calculate_constrained_y} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/contextmenu_helpers.ts';

contextmenu_calculate_submenu_translate
#

contextmenu_helpers.ts view source

contextmenu_calculate_submenu_translate(options: ContextmenuSubmenuTranslateOptions): { x: number; y: number; }

Calculates a submenu flyout's translation so it fits the layout.

Preference order on the x axis: fly out to the right of the parent menu, else flip fully to the left of it, else shift to pin whichever side overflows less. The y axis shifts up only as far as needed to fit the bottom edge.

Used by ContextmenuSubmenu.svelte.

import {contextmenu_calculate_submenu_translate} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/contextmenu_helpers.ts';

contextmenu_create_mousedown_handler
#

contextmenu_helpers.ts view source

contextmenu_create_mousedown_handler(contextmenu: ContextmenuState, get_menu_el: () => HTMLElement | undefined, open_guard?: ContextmenuOpenGuard): (e: MouseEvent) => void

Creates a mousedown handler that closes the contextmenu when pressing outside of the menu element, deferring to open_guard for presses that belong to the gesture that opened the menu: gesture presses outside don't close, and gesture presses on the menu arm the click blocker instead of activating the entry under the pointer.

Secondary-button presses outside the menu never close here - their own contextmenu event resolves the menu in the roots' handlers (reopening it elsewhere, or closing it when there's nothing to open) - with one exception: shift+rightclick, an explicit native-menu request whose contextmenu event Firefox suppresses entirely, closes on the press itself.

Registered on the window during the bubble phase deliberately - consumers keep the menu open through a press by swallowing the event (e.g. menu controller buttons that use onmousedowncapture + swallow).

import {contextmenu_create_mousedown_handler} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/contextmenu_helpers.ts';

parameters

contextmenu

: ContextmenuState
#

the contextmenu state

get_menu_el

: () => HTMLElement | undefined
#

getter for the open menu element, if any

open_guard

contextmenu_popover_attachment
#

contextmenu_helpers.ts view source

contextmenu_popover_attachment(contextmenu: ContextmenuState): Attachment<HTMLElement>

Creates an attachment that shows the contextmenu element as a manual popover, promoting it into the top layer so it paints above modal <dialog> elements (e.g. Dialog.svelte) - top-layer elements paint in insertion order.

Painting is only half of it: a modal dialog also makes everything outside its subtree inert. When the menu opens from inside a modal dialog, the menu element is reparented into that dialog (see contextmenu_resolve_popover_host) so it escapes the inert-ness and stays interactive - top-layer positioning is relative to the viewport regardless of ancestors, so the menu's fixed coordinates are unaffected. The host dialog's close also closes the menu, since the menu's DOM node vanishes with the dialog.

No-ops where the Popover API is unavailable (older browsers, jsdom), falling back to --contextmenu_z_index stacking - the menu then renders beneath and inert to any open modal dialog.

Used with the popover="manual" attribute - "manual" rather than "auto" so opening, closing, and keyboard handling stay fully owned by ContextmenuState.

import {contextmenu_popover_attachment} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/contextmenu_helpers.ts';

contextmenu_resolve_popover_host
#

contextmenu_helpers.ts view source

contextmenu_resolve_popover_host(target: HTMLElement | SVGElement | undefined): HTMLDialogElement | null

Resolves the element that must host the contextmenu popover for it to stay interactive: the modal <dialog> containing target, if any.

A modal dialog makes every element outside its subtree inert, and the top layer fixes painting order, not inertness - so a popover shown from outside the dialog paints above it but receives no pointer or focus events (hit-testing skips inert elements). Only the topmost modal dialog's subtree is interactive, so the dialog containing the menu's open target is by construction the one the menu must join.

Records a single-touch touchstart at the given coordinates. Detects a tap-then-longpress when the previous tap happened within bypass_window milliseconds and moved less than bypass_move_tolerance pixels, setting bypassed and returning true. ContextmenuItemsState
#

contextmenu_state.svelte.ts view source

Shared items state for SubmenuState and RootMenuState.

The source of truth is a plain non-reactive array because items register and unregister from component lifecycles that can interleave within a single batch - effect teardowns can observe stale signal values mid-batch, so read-copy-write against the reactive array can lose concurrent registrations (e.g. reopening the menu while it's open). Every mutation publishes an immutable snapshot, preserving the reassignment (not mutation) contract for readers.

The menu surface shared by ContextmenuRoot.svelte and ContextmenuRootForSafariCompatibility.svelte. ContextmenuOpenGuard
#

contextmenu_helpers.ts view source

Guards the menu from the residual events of the gesture that opened it, using exact gesture causality - no timing heuristics or tunable windows.

Touch: when the menu opens during a touch (the native longpress contextmenu event, or the Safari-compat custom longpress), the release of that same gesture must not interact with the menu - an unprevented touchend lets the browser synthesize compatibility mouse events (mousedown/mouseup/click) at the touch point, and the open offsets place the first menu item exactly there, activating it immediately. touchend swallows the release to stop the synthesis, and consume_blocked_click blocks the next click on the menu as belt and braces (iOS can synthesize the click regardless).

Mouse: tap-style input devices (e.g. some touchpads) can register an overlapping primary-button press during the right-click gesture that opened the menu - the compositor serializes the event stream, but the press's hardware timeStamp falls inside the gesture, and its delivery can lag long after the menu opened. Because the open offsets place the first menu item under the pointer, that press's click would activate the entry. press_belongs_to_open_gesture identifies overlap presses exactly: the press's own buttons bitmask shows the secondary button still down at generation time, or its timeStamp predates the release tracked by track_mouseup. No pressed-state is tracked across events deliberately: the native contextmenu's pointer grab swallows the secondary mouseup whenever it opens (right-click on our menu, shift+rightclick - which in Firefox doesn't even fire the contextmenu event), so a tracked flag wedges stuck, while the judged press's own buttons self-corrects. A deliberate right-then-left click - however fast - is sequential in hardware time and is never blocked.

Plain DOM-event bookkeeping with no reactive state - used only inside event handlers by ContextmenuRoot.svelte and ContextmenuRootForSafariCompatibility.svelte.

import {ContextmenuOpenGuard} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/contextmenu_helpers.ts';

members

touchstart

(): void
#

Begins a new gesture on touchstart, clearing stale flags from the previous one.

opened

(): void
#

Arms the touch release guard for the gesture that just opened the menu. Call after a successful open.

track_mouseup

(e: MouseEvent): void
#

Tracks the physical secondary button's release - call from an always-on window mouseup capture listener. The release may never be delivered (the native contextmenu's pointer grab eats it), which is why press_belongs_to_open_gesture never depends on it alone.

press_belongs_to_open_gesture

(e: MouseEvent): boolean
#

Returns true when a press belongs to the gesture that opened the menu rather than being a deliberate response to it: secondary-button presses (their own contextmenu event resolves them), presses during or predating an active touch (synthesized compatibility events), and presses overlapping the secondary button in hardware time - the press's own buttons bitmask shows the secondary button still down at generation time, or its timeStamp predates the release tracked by track_mouseup.

mousedown_on_menu

(e: MouseEvent): void
#

Handles a mousedown that landed on the menu element: when a primary-button press belongs to the opening gesture, its click is blocked from activating the entry that the open offsets placed under the pointer. Non-primary presses never arm the blocker - they produce no click, so an armed blocker would linger and eat the next deliberate click on the menu.

touchend

(e: TouchEvent): boolean
#

Handles touchend: when the release belongs to the gesture that opened the menu, swallows it (stopping mouse event synthesis) and arms the click blocker, returning true.

reset

(): void
#

Clears gesture state, including any armed click blocker. Call on touchcancel. The secondary release timestamp persists - it mirrors hardware history, not gesture state.

consume_blocked_click

(): boolean
#

Consumes an armed click blocker, returning true if the click should be swallowed. Call from the menu element's click capture handler.

create_csp_directives
#

csp.ts view source

create_csp_directives(options?: CreateCspDirectivesOptions): CspDirectives

Builds a CSP directives map for use with SvelteKit's csp.directives option (passed to sveltekit()).

Restrictive by default; opt into specific permissions via extend (append) or overrides (replace). Designed to read as an audit log: every user-added source is named at exactly one site in the source code. Library defaults are inherited unless you opt out via replace_defaults.

Validation:

  • Unknown directive keys throw.
  • Extending a ['none'] directive throws (use replace_defaults/overrides to opt in).
  • null for replace_defaults (top-level or per-key) throws — omit the option for library defaults, pass {} to start blank, or use overrides to remove a specific directive.
  • null per-key in extend throws (use overrides for removal).
  • undefined per-key is treated as omitted in all three stages.
  • Non-object entries in extend (null, undefined, primitives) throw with a friendly error.
  • Output is validated to ensure 'none' never appears alongside other tokens, that no directive ends up with an empty array (use ['none'] to forbid all), and that every source array contains only strings.

Things like rendering to a string are out of scope and left to SvelteKit.

import {create_csp_directives} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/csp.ts';

parameters

options

?: CreateCspDirectivesOptions = {}

CreateCspDirectivesOptions
#

csp.ts view source

Options for create_csp_directives.

The pipeline runs in three stages:

  1. replace_defaults sets the starting state (defaults to csp_directive_value_defaults).
  2. extend appends sources per directive, layered left to right.
  3. overrides replaces or removes per-directive values as a final pass.
import type {CreateCspDirectivesOptions} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/csp.ts';

members

replace_defaults

?: Partial<typeof csp_directive_value_defaults>
#

Starting values per directive — *wholesale replaces* the library defaults.

  • Omitted: uses csp_directive_value_defaults (the curated library defaults).
  • Provided: exactly the directives you list, nothing else inherited. Anything not listed is absent from the starting state — including security defaults like default-src: 'none'. To tweak a single directive while keeping the rest, use extend (to append) or overrides (to replace per-key) instead.
  • {}: starts blank with no directives.

null is not accepted (top-level or per-key) — omit the option to use library defaults, pass {} to start blank, or use overrides to remove a specific directive.

Per-key undefined is treated as omitted (no-op).

extend

?: readonly CspDirectiveSourcesMap[]
#

Sources to append per directive, layered left to right. Each entry is a partial map; values append to the result of replace_defaults and prior entries. Values are deduplicated within and across layers.

Only array-typed directives can be extended (boolean directives like upgrade-insecure-requests are excluded by the type). Throws if any entry attempts to extend a directive whose current value is ['none'] — use replace_defaults or overrides to opt into default-deny directives.

Per-key undefined is treated as omitted (no-op) — supports conditional patterns like {'connect-src': is_prod ? [API_URL] : undefined}. Per-key null throws — extend only appends; use overrides: { 'X': null } to remove a directive.

overrides

?: { [K in CspDirective]?: CspDirectiveValue<K> | null; }
#

Final-pass per-directive overrides. Replaces the directive value or removes it entirely. Pass null to remove a directive from the output.

Highest precedence — wins over replace_defaults and extend.

Per-key undefined is treated as omitted (no-op) — distinct from null, which removes.

csp_directive_value_defaults
#

csp.ts view source

Partial<{ "default-src": (CspActionSource | CspSource)[]; "script-src": (CspActionSource | CspSource)[]; "script-src-elem": CspSources; ... 20 more ...; sandbox: ("allow-downloads-without-user-activation" | ... 11 more ... | "allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation")[]; }>

type Partial<{ [K in CspDirective]: CspDirectiveValue<K>; }>

The library CSP directive defaults — directives enabled out of the box. Prioritizes safety but loosens around media and styles, relying on defense-in-depth. WASM compile is allowed ('wasm-unsafe-eval' on script-src and worker-src); eval is not.

Directives not listed here (report-to, require-trusted-types-for, trusted-types, sandbox) are intentionally absent by default — opt in via replace_defaults or overrides.

Customizable via CreateCspDirectivesOptions.replace_defaults.

import {csp_directive_value_defaults} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/csp.ts';

csp_directives_of_fuzdev
#

csp_of_fuzdev.ts view source

Partial<CspDirectives>

type Partial<CspDirectives>

Per-directive sources that allow full interop between fuzdev/sister sites (*.fuz.dev) — loading assets and APIs from each other, and iframing in both directions.

Pass into create_csp_directives({extend: [csp_directives_of_fuzdev]}). Intended for sites within the ecosystem; external apps usually want a narrower, hand-written allow-list.

Deliberately scoped — script-src, style-src, worker-src, etc. are not granted, even between sister sites. Add at the call site if a specific page needs them.

type_info prepared for rendering at the declaration itself. A type alias's tree carries the alias's own name at the root (type A = 'a' | 'b' → {kind: 'union', alias: 'A', members: [...]}), which typeJsonToTokens collapses to the bare name — right where A is composed into another type, circular at A's own declaration. Strips that self-alias so the root expands into its members; every other tree passes through unchanged.

DeclarationDetail
#

DeclarationDetail.svelte view source

Renders the full detail view for an exported declaration. Handles all svelte-docinfo declaration kinds (function, class, interface, type, variable, enum, component, snippet) and their kind-specific fields including parameters, props, CSS custom properties, members, overloads, external types, and more.

Each field (member, prop, parameter) is headed by its signature in the form TypeScript declares it, readonly name?: Type = default, composed from the structured data so every type links on its own (see declaration_detail.ts). A function's signature is composed the same way, and a parameter gets a row of its own only when it has more to say than that signature shows. A callable whose extraction failed (partial) keeps the flat signature. Each rendered field carries its Declaration.field fragment as an id.

import DeclarationDetail from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/DeclarationDetail.svelte';

props

declaration

: Declaration
#

see also

  • declaration.svelte.ts for the Declaration wrapper class

  • svelte-docinfo for the analysis library

dedent_continuation_lines(text: string): string

Strips the whitespace prefix that a multi-line source excerpt shares across its continuation lines, so a value broken over several source lines (a CSS custom property's fallback, a default's initializer) renders without its file's indentation. Dialog
#

Dialog.svelte view source

accepts children

Renders a native <dialog> opened with showModal(), which puts it in the top layer. The top layer escapes ancestor stacking/overflow contexts (so no Teleport is needed), traps focus, makes the rest of the page inert, closes on Escape, and restores focus to the previously focused element on close -- all natively. The dim background is the native ::backdrop.

We render a full-viewport overlay inside the dialog rather than a content-sized box, to preserve the scrolling and align="top" behaviors. The content surface itself is the consumer's -- pair this with DialogContent for the default .pane card and gutter, or render your own surface in children.

import Dialog from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/Dialog.svelte';

props

show

?: boolean = true
#

Whether the dialog is shown. When the <dialog> mounts it opens via showModal(); when it unmounts it closes. Defaults to true so the {#if opened}<Dialog>...</Dialog>{/if} pattern works without passing show -- mounting the component opens the dialog. Pass show={opened} to skip the outer {#if} and let the component manage its own conditional rendering.

align

?: DialogAlign = 'center'
#

How the content is aligned in the viewport. center vertically centers it; top aligns it to the top and grows downward, which avoids jank when the content's height changes.

dismissable

?: boolean = true
#

Whether clicking outside the content (see content_selector) closes the dialog. Escape closes it regardless of this.

content_selector

?: string = '.pane'
#

Fallback selector for a content surface you render in children yourself (rather than via DialogContent, which self-registers). When dismissable, a press that isn't inside a registered surface (e.g. DialogContent, which self-registers) and doesn't match this selector closes the dialog. Defaults to the fuz_css .pane card; set it to match your surface's outermost element -- with no registered surface and no match, presses anywhere close the dialog.

onbeforeclose

?: () => boolean | void
#

Called before a user-initiated close (Escape, click-outside, or close). Return false to veto and keep the dialog open -- e.g. to confirm discarding unsaved changes. Programmatic close via show={false} bypasses this.

onclose

?: () => void
#

Called when the dialog closes -- via Escape, click-outside, or close. Use it to sync your own open state, e.g. onclose={() => (opened = false)}. Like onbeforeclose, programmatic close via show={false} bypasses this.

children

: Snippet<[dialog: DialogContext]>
#

Rendered inside the dialog overlay. Receives the DialogContext (e.g. {close}); pair with DialogContent or render your own surface.

CSS custom properties

Properties marked inferred are found by their var() fallback or @property rule, not documented with @cssprop.

--backdrop_color

#

color of the overlay behind the dialog's content, fuz_css's global token by default

fallback var(--darken_60, #000000a6)

--shadow_color

inferred
#
fallback var(--shadow_color_umbra)

external types

Omit<SvelteHTMLElements['dialog'], 'children' | 'onclose'>

DialogContent
#

DialogContent.svelte view source

accepts children

import DialogContent from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/DialogContent.svelte';

props

padding

?: string = 'var(--space_xl)'
#

The content surface's padding, set as an inline style. Defaults to var(--space_xl) for a comfortable gutter between the card edge and its content. Set to '' or '0' for no padding (e.g. a flush image or a surface that manages its own spacing).

pane

?: boolean = true
#

Whether to apply the fuz_css .pane card class to the content surface -- its opaque background, shadow, and rounded corners. true (the default) is the standard dialog card; false gives a chromeless surface. Either way the surface registers with Dialog, so click-outside-to-close keeps working.

gutter

?: string = 'var(--space_xl3)'
#

The gutter around the .pane card -- its outer margin, and so the area outside the card where a press dismisses the dialog. Set to '' or '0' to remove.

max_width

?: string = 'var(--distance_md)'
#

The card's max width. The card shrinks to its content and is capped here, so narrow content stays narrow while wide content doesn't sprawl. Set to '' for no cap (pure shrink-to-content).

close_button

?: boolean | Snippet<[attrs: DialogCloseButtonAttrs, dialog: DialogContext]> = true
#

The close button floating just outside the content surface's top-right corner. true (the default) renders an absolutely-positioned .sized_sm.plain.icon_button that closes the dialog; false removes it. It renders after children, so a content control (or an autofocus element) takes initial focus on open rather than the close button.

Pass a Snippet to render your own. It receives attrs (DialogCloseButtonAttrs) carrying the default's placement, styling, a11y, and onclick (closes the dialog), plus the DialogContext (e.g. {close}). Spread attrs onto a <button> to inherit the corner anchoring and override only what differs (e.g. the glyph), or drop it to place the button freely. The surface is a containing block (position: relative), so an absolutely-positioned custom button anchors to it.

children

: Snippet<[dialog: DialogContext]>
#

Rendered inside the content surface. Receives the DialogContext (e.g. {close}) so content can close the dialog without reaching into Dialog's children snippet.

The default close_button renders as the surface's last child (so a content control or autofocus element wins initial focus over it). Because it's a real child, it throws off universal child-spacing selectors: your content's last element is no longer :last-child (so > :not(:last-child) matches it and > :last-child skips it), and > * + * matches the button itself. Either scope spacing to your own elements or a class, or wrap your content in a single element so its child selectors no longer see the button.

external types

Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, 'children'>

DialogContext

dialog.ts view source

Set by Dialog, read by DialogContent. Lets the content surface close the dialog without the consumer threading close through the children snippet.

import type {DialogContext} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/dialog.ts';

members

close

: (e?: Event) => void
#

Closes the dialog. When passed an event it's swallowed (default-prevented and propagation-stopped) before closing.

register_surface

: (element: Element) => () => void
#

Registers a content-surface element so a press inside it isn't treated as an outside-dismiss. The surface is known by node identity, independent of any class. Use as an attachment on the surface: {@attach register_surface}. Returns a cleanup that unregisters on unmount.

href_contains_current_page(href: string, url: Pick<URL, "href" | "origin" | "pathname">): boolean

the current page's url, e.g. SvelteKit's readonly page.url

href_is_current_page
#

page_helpers.ts view source

href_is_current_page(href: string, url: Pick<URL, "href" | "origin" | "pathname">): boolean

Whether href leads to the page at url: the same origin and pathname, with a trailing slash, the query, and the hash ignored. A relative href resolves against url, as a browser resolves it.

Library
#

library.svelte.ts view source

Rich runtime representation of a library.

Wraps LibraryJson with computed properties and provides the root of the API documentation hierarchy: Library → Module → Declaration.

A Library and everything it materializes is immutable — library_json is assigned once in the constructor — so the computed properties across all three classes are plain getters, with the allocating ones (the Module and Declaration trees, the lookup maps) cached in a private field on first read. They are deliberately not $derived: Svelte's server runtime only memoizes a $derived created during a render (ssr_context is otherwise null), so a Library constructed at module scope — the normal shape for a multi-package docs site — rebuilds its entire Module/Declaration tree on every property read, turning a declaration_by_name lookup into a full re-materialization of the library. Reactivity is at the instance level instead: swap the Library (see library_context), don't mutate one.

import {Library} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/library.svelte.ts';

library_context
#

library.svelte.ts view source

{ get: (error_message?: string | undefined) => () => Library; get_maybe: () => (() => Library) | undefined; set: (value: () => Library) => () => Library; }

Holds a getter to the active Library for the current subtree.

The getter form keeps consumers reactive when the library changes without requiring a remount — set it with a closure over reactive state, e.g. library_context.set(() => library). Components that accept a library prop (ApiIndex, ApiModule) project the prop into this context for their subtree, so descendants like ModuleLink, DeclarationLink, and TSDoc-rendered DocsLink resolve against the same library — including when an aggregator renders a foreign library that differs from the site-level context.

import {library_context} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/library.svelte.ts';

link_type_json_terminals
#

type_link.ts view source

link_type_json_terminals(tokens: TypeJsonToken[], resolves: (name: string) => boolean): TypeJsonToken[]

Splits each terminal code token of a rendered TypeJson tree at the names to_type_text_tokens finds, so the names inside terminal text (typeof A, { a: A; }, (a: A) => B) link as the same text rendered flat does. text tokens (punctuation, tuple labels) and name tokens pass through unscanned. A split name carries no module, so it resolves by name, as a flat string's names do.

import {link_type_json_terminals} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/type_link.ts';

parameters

tokens

: TypeJsonToken[]
#

the tree's tokens, from svelte-docinfo's typeJsonToTokens

resolves

: (name: string) => boolean
#

whether a candidate name is a known declaration

returns

the tokens with each linkable terminal split; their texts concatenate back to the input's

theme_state.svelte.ts view source

load_theme(themes?: Theme[], fallback?: Theme, key?: string): Theme

Loads the saved theme from storage, falling back when there's none or it doesn't resolve to a theme. A saved name loads the registry theme of that name, {name, contrast} the registry theme composed with that contrast modifier (or the registry theme alone when contrast names no modifier), an object named like a registry theme or one of its contrast compositions (ledger (high contrast)) that theme or composition (so a whole-object save from before themes saved by name loads the current version), and any other object its authored fields when they parse as a Theme.

#

local_media.svelte.ts view source

0.00001

RMS above which a mic's sample counts as heard, about -100 dBFS: below any real mic's noise floor, so only the digital silence a device sends before it starts reads lower.

LOCAL_MEDIA_PROBE_INTERVAL
#

local_media.svelte.ts view source

20

How often a starting mic's probe is read, in milliseconds.

import {LOCAL_MEDIA_PROBE_INTERVAL} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/local_media.svelte.ts';

LOCAL_MEDIA_SILENT_AFTER
#

local_media.svelte.ts view source

2000

How long a mic's track may be sendable with nothing heard before it reads silent, in milliseconds. The measured gap from a phone's track to its first non-silent sample is about 0.16 s (0.4 s to the track, 0.56 s to the sample), so 2 s is over ten times that: room for a slower device, such as a Bluetooth headset switching to its call profile, while still soon enough to tell someone why nobody hears them.

import {LOCAL_MEDIA_SILENT_AFTER} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/local_media.svelte.ts';

constructor

(options: LocalMediaOptions)
#

start

(): Promise<void>
#

Acquires the device. A no-op unless off. Resolves once the track has arrived or the start failed (see error); a mic may still be starting then, until it's heard.

stop

(): void
#

Releases the device: every track stopped, the indicator out. Abandons a start under way.

toggle

(): Promise<void>
#

Starts when off, stops otherwise.

restart

(): Promise<void>
#

Re-acquires an active source with fresh constraints, for a newly picked device. A no-op while off. It passes through off, releasing the old device before asking for the new one (break-before-make, which iOS wants, since it lets a page hold only one capture of a kind at once). A failed start leaves the source off with error set.

MediaAccessErrorReason
#

media_errors.ts view source

type "denied" | "blocked" | "not_found" | "in_use" | "overconstrained" | "aborted" | "play_refused" | "unsupported" | "ended" | "unknown"

Why a media request failed:

  • denied — the person or the browser refused the permission, or cancelled the screen picker (browsers don't tell the two apart)
  • blocked — the page may not ask at all (a permissions policy, an insecure frame)
  • not_found — no device matches
  • in_use — the device is there but couldn't be opened, usually because another app holds it
  • overconstrained — no device satisfies the constraints
  • aborted — the browser gave up for another reason
  • play_refused — the browser wouldn't start playback without a fresh gesture (its autoplay policy), so trying again from a click can work
  • unsupported — the browser doesn't offer the API here (an insecure page, or an older browser)
  • ended — a live track ended on its own: unplugged, or the permission was taken back
  • unknown — anything else
import type {MediaAccessErrorReason} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/media_errors.ts';

Re-reads the device list. A refresh that finishes after a later one started is dropped, so the list is never older than the last call.

(): Promise<void>

Re-reads the mic and camera permissions. While listening, it also follows each status's change event.

refresh

(): Promise<void>
#

Re-reads the devices and the permissions.

listen

(): () => void
#

Refreshes now and follows changes (devicechange, permission change) until the returned stop, for an $effect or onMount. A granted permission reveals labels, so the devices are re-read with it. Several components may listen at once: permissions are followed until the last one stops, and each stop counts once.

select

(kind: MediaDeviceKind, device_id: string): void
#

Picks the device for kind, the empty string for the default, and hands the picks to on_select.

selected

(kind: MediaDeviceKind): MediaDeviceInfo | null
#

The listed device picked for kind, or null for the default or a device that's away.

labeled_for

(kind: MediaDeviceKind): boolean
#

Whether the list carries real ids and labels for kind. A browser that has the mic's permission but not the camera's labels the audio devices and leaves the cameras blank, so each kind is vouched for on its own.

missing

(kind: MediaDeviceKind): boolean
#

Whether the pick for kind is known to be away: a device was picked, the list is labeled for kind, and the device isn't in it. The pick is kept, so the device is used again when it returns.

to_device_constraint

(kind: "audioinput" | "videoinput"): ConstrainDOMString | undefined
#

The deviceId constraint for the pick of kind: exact when the list vouches for it, ideal while the list can't be checked for kind (before its permission), and undefined for the default or a device that's away, so opening it never fails on a stale pick.

RemoteAudio
#

remote_audio.svelte.ts view source

The remote half of a call's audio. Construct it anywhere (it touches no browser API until unlock), call unlock from the click that joins, then add each remote stream as it arrives and remove it when it leaves. Streams added before unlock start playing at unlock.

import {RemoteAudio} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/remote_audio.svelte.ts';

members

readonly

deps

: RemoteAudioDeps
#

status

: RemoteAudioStatus
$state.raw
#
readonly

needs_resume

: boolean
$derived
#

Whether the browser paused playback and a gesture should resume it: show a prompt whose click calls resume.

context

: AudioContext | null
$state.raw
#

The context, from the first unlock until close. Share it with level probes and anything else that belongs on the call's graph, reading it each time: a context the browser closed is replaced at the next unlock, so a LocalMedia probing on it must be rebuilt after a close, or it reads silence.

readonly

can_choose_output

: boolean
#

Whether this browser can choose an output device at all.

output_device_id

: string
$state.raw
#

The output device in effect (or to apply at unlock), the empty string for the default.

output_route

: AudioOutputRoute
$state.raw
#

How sound reaches the output device.

output_error

: MediaAccessError | null
$state.raw
#

Why the last output change failed, cleared by the next one that works.

constructor

(options?: RemoteAudioOptions)
#

unlock

(): Promise<void>
#

Opens the context if there isn't one, and resumes it. Call it synchronously from a click (the Join handler), before any await: the browser allows playback only inside the gesture. Resolves once the browser has answered; status says how, and stays as it was until then. A context the browser closed is replaced by a fresh one, with every stream and the output device carried over.

resume

(): Promise<void>
#

Resumes a paused context from a later gesture, as needs_resume asks. Does nothing before the first unlock or after close, so a stray prompt can't start playback early. Also safe to try without a gesture (on returning to the page): some browsers allow it, and the rest leave needs_resume set.

add

(id: string, stream: MediaStream): void
#

Plays stream under id, typically a member's id. A new stream under a known id replaces the old one and keeps its volume and mute. A stream with no audio track yet is wired when one arrives (addtrack).

remove

(id: string): void
#

Stops playing id's stream, disconnecting its nodes. Its volume and mute are kept.

has

(id: string): boolean
#

Whether a stream is playing, or waiting to, under id.

clear

(): void
#

Removes every stream, keeping the context unlocked for the next call.

get_volume

(id: string): number
#

id's volume, 1 unless set. Reactive.

set_volume

(id: string, volume: number): void
#

Sets id's volume, 0 and up (1 as sent, above 1 louder), for now and for any later stream under id.

is_muted

(id: string): boolean
#

Whether id is muted here. Reactive.

set_muted

(id: string, muted: boolean): void
#

Mutes or unmutes id here only, keeping its volume for the unmute.

read_level

(id: string): number
#

id's level now, as RMS from 0 to 1, read before its volume and mute, so a speaking indicator shows someone muted here too. 0 for an unknown id, a stream not yet wired, or a paused context. Pair it with an AudioLevelState for a reactive indicator.

set_output

(device_id: string): Promise<RemoteAudioOutputResult>
#

Sends the call to the output device device_id, the empty string for the default. Before unlock, or once the browser closed the context (before or during the change), it's kept and applied at the next unlock. A failure sets output_error and leaves output_device_id on the device sound still plays on, except where a superseded change lands after the failure. A change superseded by a later one resolves aborted if it landed, or with its own refusal if it didn't.

close

(): void
#

Stops everything: the streams, the output route, and the context. Volumes and mutes are kept, and a later unlock opens a fresh context.

save_theme
#

theme_state.svelte.ts view source

save_theme(theme: Theme | null, themes?: Theme[], key?: string): void

Saves a theme to storage: a theme in the themes registry by its name, a registry theme composed with a contrast modifier as {name, contrast}, and any other theme whole, trimmed to its authored fields (name, summary, scheme, variables). Saving by reference means a later load takes the registry's current version, recomposed. Both matches are by name, so a theme sharing a registry theme's name saves as that registry theme, and one named like a composition (ledger (high contrast)) saves as that composition.

A composition assigned at runtime, like `theme_state.theme = compose_themes(ledger_theme, contrast_modifiers.high)`, takes the {name, contrast} path.

import {save_theme} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/theme_state.svelte.ts';

set_library_context_with_fallback(get_library_prop: () => Library | undefined, component_name: string): () => Library

SignatureToken
#

declaration_detail.ts view source

type { kind: "keyword"; text: string; } | { kind: "name"; text: string; } | { kind: "text"; text: string; } | { kind: "type"; type: string; type_info?: TypeJson; } | { kind: "value"; text: string; }

One piece of a rendered signature line. Spacing lives in the token text, so a renderer emits the tokens adjacent with nothing between them.

  • keyword - a TypeScript keyword around the name (readonly , new , extends )
  • name - the name the line declares, rendered as its heading
  • text - punctuation and parameter names
  • type - a type, with its structured tree when the analysis emitted one
  • value - a default's source text

Sparkline
#

Sparkline.svelte view source

accepts children

Renders values as a small inline SVG line graph.

Designed for comparable small multiples: pass a shared max so a set of sparklines renders at the same vertical scale instead of each stretching to fit. The stroke uses currentColor, so color it by setting color on the component or a parent (e.g. a fuz_css color_* class). Each point's stroke alpha scales with its value, from alpha_floor at 0 up to 1 at max, de-emphasizing quiet stretches.

scale controls only the geometry: the nonlinear options compress the top of the range so small values stay legible under a large shared max, while the alpha fade keeps tracking the linear ratio so it still encodes true magnitude.

import Sparkline from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/Sparkline.svelte';

props

values

: number[]
#

max

?: number
#

The value rendered at full height and full alpha. Pass a shared max across sparklines for comparable scales. Defaults to the local max of values.

scale

?: SparklineScale = 'linear'
#

Vertical scale for the line's geometry — see SparklineScale. The alpha fade always tracks the linear ratio regardless of scale.

width

Width of the svg in px.

Height of the svg in px.

SvgData
#

svg.ts view source

A structured icon definition rendered by Svg.svelte. Rendering is purely structural - typed fields, never raw markup - so untrusted data cannot introduce script execution or navigation. See Svg.svelte for the full security notes, including the residual style url(...) caveat.

import type {SvgData} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/svg.ts';

members

paths

?: ({ d: string; } & SVGAttributes<SVGPathElement>)[] | null
#

List of svg path attribute objects, spread onto each path element. The d attribute is required; a per-path fill overrides the resolved fill.

style

?: string | null
#

Inline style applied to the root svg element, merged with any style passed as a component prop. Travels with the icon definition - per-instance svg attributes belong on the Svg component itself.

fill

?: string | null
#

Default fill for every path, falling back to var(--text_color, #000). Overridden by the component's fill prop, and per-path by a path's own fill.

label

?: string | null
#

Accessible name, applied as aria-label. Overridden by the component's label prop.

viewBox

?: string | null
#

Defaults to "0 0 100 100".

gradients

?: SvgGradient[] | null

Gradient definitions rendered into the svg's <defs> block. This is the structured replacement for raw markup - reference a gradient from a path/shape fill or stroke with url(#id). Most svgs need only paths.

to_member_signature_tokens
#

declaration_detail.ts view source

to_member_signature_tokens(member: MemberJsonInput, options?: MemberSignatureOptions): SignatureToken[]

Composes a member's line after the way TypeScript declares it: readonly name?: Type = default for a property, name<T>(a: A): R for a method, constructor(a: A) for a class constructor, and the bare (a: A): R or new (a: A): R for an unnamed call or construct signature. A function-typed property reads now: () => number where the data marks it (property) and has one signature, or handler: Handler where it's written with a named function type (its typeInfo); unmarked, or with overloads, which the method form lists one by one, it reads now(): number. A name that needs quotes gets single ones, whatever the source wrote.

The name is followed by the flat typeSignature instead where composing would lose something: a callable whose extraction failed (partial), and a construct signature (which carries no structured return type).

import {to_member_signature_tokens} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/declaration_detail.ts';

to_type_text_tokens
#

type_link.ts view source

to_type_text_tokens(type: string, resolves: (name: string) => boolean): TypeTextToken[]

Splits a flat type string into the names that resolve and the text around them, for type text svelte-docinfo emits with no structure: a flat string with no tree beside it, and a tree's terminal text (object and function types, and source text such as typeof a or keyof A). (a: A) => B can then link A and B independently.

The scan is lexical, not a parse. It skips what plainly isn't a type reference: TypeScript's keywords, string and template literals whole (so a template's ${A} doesn't link), comments, a property access's right side (ns.Name: a dotted chain links its head, or, when the head resolves nowhere, its last name, so typeof specs.a_spec over a namespace import links a_spec), and a property or parameter name (name: and name?:, written with no space before the colon, unlike a conditional type's ? A : B). A name in another non-type position (a method key, a binding name, a type parameter) still links when a declaration happens to share it.

import {to_type_text_tokens} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/type_link.ts';

parameters

type

: string
#

the flat type string

resolves

: (name: string) => boolean
#

whether a candidate name is a known declaration

returns

the tokens in order, adjacent text merged; their texts concatenate back to type

TypeJsonView
#

TypeJsonView.svelte view source

Renders svelte-docinfo's structured TypeJson tree as inline code: reference nodes (and alias-carrying unions/intersections) link to API docs via DeclarationLink when the name resolves in the library — scoped to the token's declaring module when the analysis names one — terminal type text is syntax-highlighted via fuz_code's Code, with the declaration names inside it linked as TypeLink links a flat string (link_type_json_terminals), and structural punctuation comes from svelte-docinfo's typeJsonToTokens, which owns spacing and parenthesization so rendering is whitespace-exact.

The structured sibling of TypeLink, which renders flat type strings — TypeLink delegates here when given type_info, and svelte-docinfo omits the tree wherever the flat string is the whole story, so the two compose as "structured when it says something, flat otherwise". Pass title (typically the flat sibling string) to keep the expansion reachable on hover where the tree replaced it with a recovered name.

import TypeJsonView from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/TypeJsonView.svelte';

: TypeJson
#

?: string

accepts children

Renders a type reference, linking the parts that resolve to library declarations.

With type_info it delegates to TypeJsonView, which renders the structured tree — reference names become DeclarationLinks, as do the names inside its terminal text, and everything else is syntax-highlighted in place, so Map<string, Tome> | null links Map and Tome independently, with the flat type as hover text. Without it the type string links whole when it names a declaration outright, and otherwise by the names found in it (to_type_text_tokens), so a function type's (a: Options) => Result still links Options and Result.

import TypeLink from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/TypeLink.svelte';

type

: string
#

type_info

?: TypeJson
#

Structured type tree, when svelte-docinfo emitted one beside the flat string — rendered via TypeJsonView (per-node linkification, with type as hover text) instead of the string matching below. An absent tree falls through to type, so call sites pass both fields unconditionally. hash and the rest/a_attrs/code_attrs attributes apply only to the flat branches, not the delegated tree.

hash

?: string
#

URL fragment for a whole-string declaration link, with or without the #.

a_attrs

?: HTMLAnchorAttributes
#

Anchor attributes, applied only when the whole type resolves to a declaration link.

code_attrs

?: HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>
#

Code attributes, applied to the code root when the whole type doesn't resolve.

url_to_root_relative(url: string, origin?: string): string

Convert a full URL to root-relative format by removing the origin.

Uses SvelteKit's page state for the current origin by default.

import {url_to_root_relative} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/library_helpers.ts';

?: string = page.url.origin

examples

// Assuming page.url.origin is 'https://fuz.dev' url_to_root_relative('https://fuz.dev/docs/api') // => '/docs/api'

import type {VitePluginPkgJsonOptions} from '@fuzdev/fuz_ui/vite_plugin_pkg_json.ts';

members

keys

?: readonly (keyof PackageJson)[]
#

The package.json fields to keep in the served subset. Defaults to the curated, publish-safe pkg_json_keys. Pass a wider list — usually `` [...pkg_json_keys, 'extra'] `` — to expose more fields; the same list must reach library_json_from_modules (see the module comment).
